First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{4}-\frac{3}{y}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{4})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1}) \\  & =4{y}^{3}-3(-{y}^{-2}) \\  & =4{y}^{3}+3{y}^{-2} \\  & =4{y}^{3}+\frac{3}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{5}+3}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4{y}^{5}+3}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(4,-1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,-1)} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}}{4(-1)^{5}+3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$
